<!-- pr-reviewer: 86f73eba91a81ac9ec86333eba1ea38f5e102a39 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**: at the next minor cut. This is a `fix(contour)!` breaking change (the posted direction and G41/G42 change), so it waits for the cut and does not merge between cuts.

Safety-tier review. I trial-merged the PR with `upstream/main` (clean, no conflicts) in its own worktree and built it there. I checked the direction and compensation rules from first principles, against the code and against the posted goldens.

### Direction and compensation, checked from first principles
With an M3 spindle (clockwise seen from +Z), climb milling means the tooth enters at full chip thickness. That puts the material on the RIGHT of the travel and the cutter to the LEFT of the contour, which is G41 (RS-274 / ISO 6983: G41 = cutter left of the contour along the travel).

| Case | Climb (M3) | Conventional | Where I checked it in this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| Outside / boss, closed | CW, G41 | CCW, G42 | `contour_control_comp.nc` (fanuc/haas/mazak/840D): (5,0)→(0,0)→(0,10)→(10,10)→(10,0) is CW, `G41`; the 840D comp golden posts `G41 NORM`. Ring shoelace on `contour_plate_with_hole` / `disc_hole` / `tangential_lead`: outer ring area < 0 (CW), corners `G02` |
| Inside / hole wall, closed | CCW, G41 | CW, G42 | Same goldens: hole ring area > 0 (CCW), walls `G03`. `contour_inside_shrinks_and_flips_travel` and `conventional_inside_travels_reversed` |
| Wear comp | CW outside, G41 | - | `contour_wear_comp.nc` (fanuc/haas/mazak/840D): `G41`, corners all `G02` |
| Open contour | material right of travel | reversed | `contour_open::open_run`: the offset tube is CCW with the chain on its left, so reversing puts the material on the right. Pinned by `area_open::the_open_pass_runs_climb_with_the_material_on_its_right` |
| 2D Chamfer | boss CW, bore CCW | reversed | `walked(l, climb == inside, false)`; `chamfer_climb_keeps_the_material_right` |
| Inch | same as mm | | `inch/{fanuc,haas,mazak,doosan-dnm,sinumerik,tormach}/contour_plate_with_hole.nc`: same orientation and arc split as the mm set |
| Heidenhain (ISO form, absolute `I`/`J` centre blocks) | same | | `heidenhain/contour_plate_with_hole.nc`: CW outer ring with `G02` corners on the right centres, hole `G03` |
| M4 | not claimed | | Mill ops never post M4. Only `OpParams::Thread { spindle_reverse }` does (`posting.rs:1078`). The decision file says that every climb rule must read the spindle if a mill op ever gains M4. That is correct scoping. |

`air_side` (climb: air = left normal `(-t.y, t.x)`), `side_of` (climb → `CompSide::Left`), `Legal::air_left = Some(climb)` and `contour_comp_room::arcs` (`left = p.climb`, over the walk `push_span` orients to the travel at `contour_comp.rs:253-262`) all follow from the same rule. `ring::walked` cannot underflow (`s + n - k` with `k < n`, and it returns early when `n == 0`).

### What looks good
- One rule (`climb == inside` walks the stored ring forward) replaces the XOR in both places in `contour.rs`, and in the chamfer. The seam is held by `ring::walked`, so climb and conventional differ only in direction.
- The keep-down ring-to-ring link is now proved against both rings' leads. The climb case lifts with a note instead of posting a crossing.
- The `push_arc_in` sliver guard is tight: it skips the split only when the extremum lands on the lattice copy of an end.
- Each new pin checks its outcome with its own measurements (signed sweep, posted words, and the app-level analytic-solid gouge scan with verify). No pins were deleted. New test files carry provenance and gate maps.
- The body states BREAKING, and the `Changelog:` line says "BREAKING: posted direction reverses…". `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched, as are snapshot PNGs and process files. The decision is in `docs/decisions/1555-climb-direction.md`. The commit subjects are conventional, with `!` on the fix.

### Goldens (spot-checked by script, not by eye)
- **Arc centres:** I replayed every changed mm, inch and dialect NC golden (`G2`/`G3` with incremental `I`/`J`), checking start radius against end radius about the stated centre. 0 mismatches in 36 files. The worst error is 0.001 mm, which is rounding at 3 decimals. None of the swaps is a letter-only flip: each `G2`↔`G3` comes with new `I`/`J`. For example, the hole lead in `contour_disc_hole.nc` changed from `G02 … I-1.998 J0.098` to `G03 X19.853 Y7.005 I1.998 J-0.098`.
- **Endpoints:** the old and new goldens share the same seam and the same ring vertices. The lead-in and lead-out endpoints swap (e.g. the hole lead now starts at (17.953, 9.1), the old lead-out end). The fitted arc split points on the round hole differ (22.711/11.282 vs 22.645/11.414); both sit on the r = 3 tool-centre circle.
- **Leads:** every lead arc I traced is on the air side and tangent at the join. Hole: the R2 lead circle is centred 1.0 from the bore axis, so it stays inside the r = 3 centre ring. Outer: the lead arcs sweep below y = -2.98. Control comp: ramp-on (11,-3)→(5,0) and ramp-off (5,0)→(-1,-3) are both in air below the part, and 6.7 mm is longer than the 3 mm radius. The comp seam moved from (10,5) to (5,0). That is harmless, but it means "seams stay put" does not cover the comp path.
- **Corner chord:** the 0.346 mm `G01` chord at the outer ring's (40,0) corner sags 0.005 mm toward the part. The old golden had the same chord at the other end of the ring, so the direction reversal added nothing.

### Local results (merged with main d00243a, macOS, debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| build: `cargo test --no-run` for cl, motion, post, app | ok |
| motion: lib + 73 suites (all except slow finish3d/pivot5d/flow), incl. `climb_direction` 9/9, `control_comp` 8, `wear_comp` 2, `level_links` 12, `machining2d` 66, `one_descent`, `vertical_arc_entry` | 830 passed, 0 failed, 16 ignored |
| app: 29 suites: `climb_direction` 2/2, `golden_cl` 32, `solid_law_goldens` 7, `control_comp` 5, `wear_comp` 5, `area_open` 11, `level_links` 7, `thread_boss` 12, `thread_mill` 8, `recorded_post_streams` 5, `posting` 17, `verify` 21, `wall_arc_entry` 7, `lead_approach` 6, `arc_entry` 3, `contour_start_point` 8, `program_units` 7, `project_roundtrip` 73, `roughing2d` 7, … | 307 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored |
| app lib 208, `mcp` 22, `operations` 119 (6 ignored), `conformance` 7; post crate (all suites incl. `recorded_streams` 12, `vertical_arc_entry` 3) + cl crate | 860 passed, 0 failed, 6 ignored (59 binaries) |
| ui lib (cwd `crates/ui`) | 741 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Mutation checks (my own run; each change reverted afterwards)
| Mutation | Red |
|---|---|
| `side_of` back to climb = G42 | 8 (motion `control_compensation_posts_g41…`, `the_side_follows_the_travel…`, `computer_is_the_default…`, `wear_walks…`; app fanuc/haas/mazak/840D control + wear golden tests) |
| `walked` rule `climb == inside` → `!=` (both sites) | 25 (all `climb_direction` direction pins, motion lib `contour_inside_shrinks…` / `conventional_inside…`, app `the_2d_contour_runs_clockwise…`, 4 CL goldens, `every_posted_golden_is_a_program_the_gate_passes`, keep-down links, comp) |
| `air_side` back to climb = air right | 13 (`arc_leads_stay_tangent_after_the_flip`, `arc_lead_enters_as_a_quarter_arc`, `tangential_lead_enters_parallel_and_lands_g1`, 4 CL goldens, keep-down links, comp) |
| open-contour reversal removed | 1 (`area_open::the_open_pass_runs_climb_with_the_material_on_its_right`) |
| `contour_comp_room::arcs` back to `tool_left(p)` | 1 (`control_comp::stock_to_leave_rides_the_programmed_contour_not_the_register`) |

### #1579 and the `climb: false` UI test
I set `arc_moves_draw_curved` back to `climb: true` locally to check this claim. It goes red because the feed moves are drawn as flagged (verify `Gouge`), not green. Generation warnings ride the posted stream as `WARN` (`posting.rs:494`), and `post_program` refuses on any warning (`posting.rs:563`, "post blocked - …"). So the 0.01 mm arc sag at the user's coarse 0.1 tolerance is caught and held, never posted silently. It is a fitter defect (the split depends on the walk direction), with a workaround (a finer tolerance). Pinning the draw-law test on the conventional walk is acceptable, and P3 is the right rating for #1579.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. With `air_side` reverted, `leads_stay_on_the_air_side_after_the_flip` stayed green, as did the app-level `the_2d_contour_runs_clockwise…`. The lead-legality net rebuilds or refuses a lead that would enter the part, so those tests check the outcome, not the rule. The rule is pinned by the tangency, quarter-arc and golden tests above. That is fine, but the pin's name claims more than it isolates.
2. The `comp_room::arcs` fix is pinned by one indirect test. I also probed the conventional + Inside + R2 fillet under a Ø10 tool with control comp. It is refused both with and without the fix, because another room check catches it. A direct four-case pin (outside/inside × climb/conventional, with a tight inside arc) would make the "1 of 4" fix visible. It could ride #1579 or a P7 issue.
3. 2D Chamfer `Side::Auto` is read as a boss. That is right when the picked region holds the hole as an inner loop of material. A bore picked as an air region under Auto would run conventional while climb is set. That is a finish-quality issue, not a gouge, since the chamfer ride's circle is direction-free. `inside` exists only in the motion-runtime `ChamferParams`, which has no serde. The project-level `side` field already exists, so there is no format change, no migration and no new MCP parameter.
4. Files already over ~400 lines grew a little: `machining2d/contour.rs` 442 → 445, `cl/path.rs` 413 → 417, `operation/generate.rs` 3457 → 3462.
5. Release notes must list this first as breaking (post output). The `Changelog:` line already says so.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** This is a breaking change: existing projects will post with reversed direction and swapped G41/G42, so the merge is the maintainer's call at the cut.

Safety-tier review of the posted direction and compensation side, checked from first principles (M3, tool left of travel = climb = G41; outside profile clockwise, inside counter-clockwise, seen from +Z). A collaborator review with this marker already exists for this head and reaches the same verdict; this one is independent and adds the runner result.

**What looks good**
- `contour_control_comp.nc`: the square now runs CW (5,0 -> 0,0 -> 0,10 -> 10,10 -> 10,0) under G41, so the tool stays outside the part, on the same side as the old CCW/G42 run. Lead-in (11,-3 -> 5,0) and the G40 exit (-1,-3) are both outside the part.
- `contour_wear_comp.nc`: the same 3 mm offset ring as before, now CW with G41; arc centres are right (G02 X-3 Y0 I0 J3 is about (0,0)).
- `haas/contour_tangential_lead.nc`: outside ring CW, hole ring CCW; the lead arc ends tangent to the first wall segment (checked from I/J), sits in air below the bottom edge, and the lead-out mirrors it. Seams are kept, so only direction and lead side differ.
- `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc`: the boss roughing contour changes G03 to G02 over the same points reversed. That is the boss-edge climb rule; thread passes and the thread hand law are untouched.
- `vertical_arc_{x,y,oblique}.cl` post inputs: same geometry, ring order reversed; arc-entry lines unchanged. The reason is stated in the PR.
- No snapshot PNG, CHANGELOG or PROCESS_VERSION edit. Title has `!`, there is a `Changelog:` line stating the break, `Fixes` line, and a decision file `docs/decisions/1555-climb-direction.md`. New pins come with a mutation table.

**Results merged with main**
- On the self-hosted runner: https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runs/43523217842 - success, merged with main 45a76e1. Quick gate: 9 steps, 0 failed, 22.6 min (geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion, app, ui suites, gate clippy). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Not run locally: the diff has no `cfg(windows)` or per-OS pinned lines.

**Requested before merge**
- None.

**Questions / notes (not blocking)**
1. `crates/ui/src/law_tests.rs` (`arc_moves_draw_curved`) now runs on the conventional walk. Finding: on a tessellated 30 mm cylinder at 0.1 mm tolerance, the climb walk's arc fit sits about 0.01 mm past the wall. The split points depend on the walk direction. Verify flags a gouge, so the post is held, not silent, but the overlay draws it red instead of green. A finer tolerance is the workaround. The follow-up is #1579 (P3).
2. Chamfer `Side::Auto` is read as a boss edge; a bore edge needs `Side: Inside` to climb CCW.
3. Release notes must list this first as breaking (post output); a project that set `climb: false` as a workaround now posts conventional.
4. I read the compensation, tangential-lead, bore-arc-entry, thread-mill and post-input diffs by hand; the other golden files follow the same swap-and-mirror pattern. Left-hand spindle is not supported for mill ops, so it was not checked.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
